source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substring including written/read and other annotations.
source.public_versification_note: Exact XML records mapped to public labels; Zechariah 1:18–2:13 and Malachi 4 have different Hebrew chapter boundaries.

delta_method: F0 retained; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential choices flagged by the selective apparatus. Classification remains provisional. Overlap is triage only, with no change quota.

comparative_references.scope: Programmatic alignment after recovery of unfinished original-language drafts; selected bilingual rereads recorded separately. TSW is not the base text.

verses.rationale: Retains the precise date, both patronymics, and distinct offices.
verses.before: In the second year of King Darius, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came by the hand of Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest:
verses.after: In the second year of King Darius, on the first day of the sixth month, the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest:
verses.tsw_comparator: In the second year of King Darius, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came by the hand of Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest:

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated time in the people’s quoted excuse.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “These people say, ‘The time has not yet come to rebuild the house of the LORD.’”
verses.after: The LORD of Armies says, “These people say, ‘The time has not come—the time to rebuild the LORD’s house.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “These people say, ‘The time has not yet come to rebuild the house of the LORD.’”

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated prophetic messenger introduction.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD came by the hand of Haggai the prophet:
verses.after: Then the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD came by the hand of Haggai the prophet:

verses.rationale: Keeps the emphatic you and the contrast between private houses and this house.
verses.before: “Is it a time for you yourselves to dwell in your paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins?
verses.after: “Is it time for you yourselves to live in paneled houses while this house lies in ruins?”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Is it a time for you yourselves to dwell in your paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins?

verses.rationale: Gives the set-your-heart idiom a repeatable natural rendering.
verses.before: Now therefore, thus says the LORD of Hosts: Consider your ways.
verses.after: Now the LORD of Armies says, “Think carefully about your ways.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore, thus says the LORD of Hosts: Consider your ways.

verses.rationale: Retains all five frustrated activities and the concrete leaking-bag image.
verses.before: You have sown much and harvested little. You eat, but never have enough. You drink, but never become filled. You clothe yourselves, but no one is warm. And he who earns wages earns wages to put them into a bag with holes.”
verses.after: You sow much but bring in little. You eat but never have enough. You drink but are not filled. You put on clothes but are not warm. Those who earn wages put them into a bag full of holes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You have sown much and harvested little. You eat, but never have enough. You drink, but never become filled. You clothe yourselves, but no one is warm. And he who earns wages earns wages to put them into a bag with holes.”

verses.rationale: Repeats the exact wording of the recurring summons.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Consider your ways.
verses.after: The LORD of Armies says, “Think carefully about your ways.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Consider your ways.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three commands and the read be-honored form.
verses.before: Go up to the hills and bring wood and rebuild the house, that I may take pleasure in it and be glorified,” says the LORD.
verses.after: Go up into the hills, bring timber, and rebuild the house. Then I will take pleasure in it and be honored,” says the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Go up to the hills and bring wood and rebuild the house, that I may take pleasure in it and be glorified,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the surprising divine action and the house/house contrast.
verses.before: “You looked for much, and behold, it came to little. And when you brought it home, I blew it away. Why?” declares the LORD of Hosts. “Because of my house, which lies in ruins, while each of you runs to his own house.
verses.after: “You expected much, but look—there was little. You brought it home, and I blew it away. Why?” declares the LORD of Armies. “Because my house lies in ruins while each of you runs to his own house.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You looked for much, and behold, it came to little. And when you brought it home, I blew it away. Why?” declares the LORD of Hosts. “Because of my house, which lies in ruins, while each of you runs to his own house.

verses.rationale: Keeps both withholding clauses and dew rather than generalizing to rain.
verses.before: So the heavens above you have withheld the dew, and the earth has withheld its produce.
verses.after: That is why the heavens above you have withheld dew and the earth has withheld its produce.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore the heavens above you have withheld the dew, and the earth has withheld its produce.

verses.rationale: Retains the full list of affected crops, creatures, and labor.
verses.before: I have called for a drought upon the land and the hills, upon the grain, the new wine, the oil, upon what the ground brings forth, upon man and beast, and upon all their labor.”
verses.after: I called for drought on the land and the hills, on grain, new wine, and oil, on everything the ground produces, on humans and animals, and on all the work of your hands.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And I have called for a drought upon the land and the hills, upon the grain, the new wine, the oil, upon what the ground brings forth, upon man and beast, and upon all their labor.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the two leaders and remnant together and all three divine-name occurrences.
verses.before: Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, and Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the LORD their God and the words of Haggai the prophet, because the LORD their God had sent him. And the people feared the LORD.
verses.after: Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Joshua son of Jehozadak the high priest, and all the remnant of the people listened to the voice of the LORD their God and to the words of Haggai the prophet, whom the LORD their God had sent. The people feared the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, and Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the LORD their God and the words of Haggai the prophet, because the LORD their God had sent him. And the people feared the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the messenger/message wordplay and repeated sender identification.
verses.before: Then Haggai, the messenger of the LORD, spoke to the people with the LORD's message: “I am with you,” declares the LORD.
verses.after: Haggai, the LORD’s messenger, delivered the LORD’s message to the people: “I am with you,” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Haggai, the messenger of the LORD, spoke to the people with the LORD's message: “I am with you,” declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains each spirit separately and lets the sentence continue into its date.
verses.before: And the LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people. And they came and worked on the house of the LORD of Hosts, their God,
verses.after: The LORD stirred the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people. They came and worked on the house of the LORD of Armies, their God,
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people. And they came and worked on the house of the LORD of Hosts, their God,

verses.rationale: Keeps the closing work date complete and attached to the preceding action.
verses.before: on the twenty-fourth day of the month, in the sixth month, in the second year of King Darius.
verses.after: on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of King Darius.
verses.tsw_comparator: on the twenty-fourth day of the month, in the sixth month, in the second year of King Darius.

verses.rationale: Retains the exact second date and messenger formula.

verses.rationale: Preserves the three addressees and their formal titles.
verses.before: “Speak now to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the remnant of the people, saying,
verses.after: “Speak to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the remnant of the people. Say:

verses.rationale: Makes the three questions natural without softening the comparison.
verses.before: ‘Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? And how do you see it now? Is it not as nothing in your eyes?
verses.after: ‘Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? How does it look to you now? Does it not seem like nothing in your eyes?
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? And how do you see it now? Is it not as nothing in your eyes?

verses.rationale: Preserves all three be-strong commands and all three declarations.
verses.before: Yet now be strong, O Zerubbabel,’ declares the LORD. ‘Be strong, O Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land,’ declares the LORD. ‘Work, for I am with you,’ declares the LORD of Hosts,
verses.after: But now, be strong, Zerubbabel,’ declares the LORD. ‘Be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land,’ declares the LORD. ‘Get to work, for I am with you,’ declares the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet now be strong, O Zerubbabel,’ declares the LORD. ‘Be strong, O Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land,’ declares the LORD. ‘Work, for I am with you,’ declares the LORD of Hosts,

verses.rationale: Keeps the compressed covenant-word construction, exodus reference, and abiding spirit.
verses.before: ‘according to the covenant that I made with you when you came out of Egypt. My Spirit stands in your midst. Do not fear.’
verses.after: ‘This is the word I covenanted with you when you came out of Egypt, and my spirit remains among you. Do not be afraid.’
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘according to the covenant that I made with you when you came out of Egypt. My Spirit stands in your midst. Do not fear.’

verses.rationale: Retains the time qualification and all four cosmic realms.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD of Hosts: ‘Yet once more, in a little while, I will shake the heavens and the earth and the sea and the dry land.
verses.after: For the LORD of Armies says, ‘Once more, in a little while, I will shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD of Hosts: ‘Yet once more, in a little while, I will shake the heavens and the earth and the sea and the dry land.

verses.rationale: Reads the desired things collectively with the plural verb, without imposing a personal messianic referent.
verses.before: I will shake all nations, and the treasures of all nations shall come in, and I will fill this house with glory,’ says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: I will shake all the nations, and the treasures of all the nations will come. I will fill this house with glory,’ says the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I will shake all nations, and the treasures of all nations shall come in, and I will fill this house with glory,’ says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Keeps both mine clauses and the material treasure connection.
verses.before: ‘The silver is mine, and the gold is mine,’ declares the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: ‘The silver is mine, and the gold is mine,’ declares the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘The silver is mine, and the gold is mine,’ declares the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Retains this house, comparative glory, peace, and both declarations.
verses.before: ‘The latter glory of this house shall be greater than the former,’ says the LORD of Hosts. ‘And in this place I will give peace,’ declares the LORD of Hosts.”
verses.after: ‘The later glory of this house will be greater than the former,’ says the LORD of Armies. ‘And in this place I will give peace,’ declares the LORD of Armies.”
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘The latter glory of this house shall be greater than the former,’ says the LORD of Hosts. ‘And in this place I will give peace,’ declares the LORD of Hosts.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the third dated message exact.

verses.rationale: Retains the priests’ role in giving instruction rather than reducing it to opinion.

verses.after: The LORD of Armies says, “Ask the priests for instruction:

verses.rationale: Keeps the indirect-contact distinction essential to the question and the full food list.
verses.before: If someone carries holy meat in the fold of his garment, and with the fold touches bread, or stew, or wine, or oil, or any kind of food, does it become holy?” The priests answered and said, “No.”
verses.after: ‘If someone carries holy meat in the fold of his garment, and that fold touches bread, stew, wine, oil, or any food, does the food become holy?’” The priests answered, “No.”
verses.tsw_comparator: If someone carries holy meat in the fold of his garment, and with the fold touches bread, or stew, or wine, or oil, or any kind of food, does it become holy?” The priests answered and said, “No.”

verses.rationale: Distinguishes direct corpse-related uncleanness from the previous indirect holiness transfer.
verses.before: Then Haggai said, “If one who is unclean by contact with a dead body touches any of these, does it become unclean?” The priests answered and said, “It becomes unclean.”
verses.after: Haggai asked, “If someone made unclean by a dead body touches any of these, does it become unclean?” The priests answered, “It becomes unclean.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Haggai said, “If one who is unclean by contact with a dead body touches any of these, does it become unclean?” The priests answered and said, “It becomes unclean.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the divine first-person assessment and the relation to offerings.
verses.before: Then Haggai answered and said, “So is this people, and so is this nation before me,” declares the LORD, “and so is every work of their hands. And what they offer there is unclean.
verses.after: Then Haggai said, “That is how these people and this nation are before me,” declares the LORD. “So is all the work of their hands, and what they offer there is unclean.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Haggai answered and said, “So is this people, and so is this nation before me,” declares the LORD, “and so is every work of their hands. And what they offer there is unclean.

verses.rationale: Preserves the temporal hinge while signaling the retrospective comparison that follows.
verses.before: Now then, consider from this day onward. Before stone was placed upon stone in the temple of the LORD,
verses.after: Now think carefully, from this day onward, about the time before stone was laid on stone in the LORD’s temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now then, consider from this day onward. Before stone was placed upon stone in the temple of the LORD,

verses.rationale: Preserves all four numbers while leaving the source’s unstated units nonspecific.
verses.before: how did you fare? When one came to a heap of twenty measures, there were but ten. When one came to the wine vat to draw fifty measures, there were but twenty.
verses.after: When someone came to a heap expecting twenty measures, there were ten. When someone came to the wine vat to draw fifty, there were twenty.
verses.tsw_comparator: how did you fare? When one came to a heap of twenty measures, there were but ten. When one came to the wine vat to draw fifty measures, there were but twenty.

verses.rationale: Retains the three afflictions and supplies the return verb demanded by the elliptical relational clause.

verses.after: I struck you and all the work of your hands with blight, mildew, and hail, yet you did not turn to me,” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: I struck you and all the work of your hands with blight and mildew and hail, yet you did not turn to me,” declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated summons and exact foundation date.

verses.after: “Think carefully, from this day onward—from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, from the day the foundation of the LORD’s temple was laid. Think carefully!
verses.tsw_comparator: Consider from this day onward, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month. Since the day that the foundation of the LORD's temple was laid, consider:

verses.rationale: Retains the question, all four plants, and the promise before visible yield.

verses.after: Is there still seed in the storehouse? The vine, fig tree, pomegranate, and olive tree have not yet borne fruit. From this day on, I will bless you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Is the seed yet in the barn? Indeed, the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, and the olive tree have yielded nothing. But from this day on I will bless you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated overturning and the fratricidal ending.
